name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+12 partisan lean favors Fallon strongly
Fallon's huge financial edge: $1.1M on hand vs. Pearce's ~$2K
Prediction markets price Fallon at ~96% to win
Incumbency advantage with no polling to suggest a race
model.rationale: Fallon combines a solidly Republican district, a large cash advantage, and near-certain market pricing, while Pearce has raised almost nothing. No polls or expert ratings show any sign of competition, so the race stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Pearce within single digits or unexpected outside spending against Fallon would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pat Fallon seeks another term in this northeast Texas district, which leans Republican by about twelve points. He enters the general election with a renomination secured, roughly $1.1 million in cash, and modest outside support, while Democrat Jason Pearce has raised about $16,000 and has minimal resources. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Fallon roughly a 96 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point clearly to Fallon: the district lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor him, with no evidence of a competitive race emerging. Pearce would need a dramatic shift in the political environment or a surge of outside investment to make this close, and nothing in the available evidence suggests either is happening.
